t: In marketing terminology, a 'demand' differs from a 'want' in that a demand is:
o: A basic human requirement such as food or safety
A want shaped by culture and personality
A want backed by the ability and willingness to pay
A product feature requested by a customer
e: Needs are basic requirements, wants are needs shaped by culture and individuality, and demands are wants supported by purchasing power.

t: In a SWOT analysis conducted by a private life insurer, 'the growing share of digitally literate young earners in Tier-2 cities' would be classified as:
o: An opportunity
A threat
A weakness
A strength
e: Strengths and weaknesses are internal to the firm; opportunities and threats arise in the external environment, and a growing receptive market is an opportunity.

topic: Insurance Market and Marketing Environment in India
t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was established as a statutory body under an Act passed in:
e: The IRDA Act, 1999 created the regulator (renamed IRDAI in 2014) and opened the sector to private insurers from 2000.

topic: Insurance Market and Marketing Environment in India
t: The abolition of tariffs in Indian general insurance with effect from 1 January 2007 (detariffing) changed the marketing environment because insurers could thereafter:
o: Sell life and general insurance under a single licence
Stop paying commission to agents
Dispense with IRDAI approval for all products
Set their own premium rates for most classes, making price a competitive variable
e: Detariffing freed pricing for fire, engineering, motor own-damage and other classes (motor third-party rates remained regulated), shifting competition from service alone to price and service.

topic: Insurance Market and Marketing Environment in India
t: Insurance penetration of a country is measured as:
o: Number of policies per 1,000 persons
Sum assured as a percentage of national savings
Total premium as a percentage of gross domestic product
Premium per head of population
e: Penetration is premium to GDP; premium per capita is insurance density. India's penetration has been around 3.7% in recent years, well below the world average.

t: The three components of an attitude in the tri-component model are:
o: Cognitive, affective and conative
Awareness, trial and adoption
Cultural, social and personal
Rational, emotional and habitual
e: Cognition is belief or knowledge, affect is feeling, and conation is the tendency to act; a campaign may target any one component to change attitudes towards insurance.

t: Which of the following statements about the purchase of life insurance is most accurate from a consumer-behaviour perspective?
o: It is a low-involvement routine purchase decided mainly by habit
It is a variety-seeking purchase in which customers frequently switch brands
It is a high-involvement purchase with extended problem solving because of its cost, duration and complexity
It is an impulse purchase triggered by point-of-sale displays
e: High cost, long commitment and perceived risk make life insurance a high-involvement decision requiring information search and advice.

t: When a young professional buys the same health insurer's policy as his colleagues because they speak highly of it, the colleagues are acting as a:
o: Market segment
Reference group
Distribution channel
Buying centre
e: A reference group is a group whose values and behaviour serve as a point of comparison; peer groups strongly influence insurance choice because the product is hard to evaluate.

t: A moderator leads a two-hour discussion among eight recently insured customers to explore why they chose their insurer. This research technique is:
o: A structured survey
An experiment
A focus group
Observation
e: Focus groups are a qualitative exploratory technique; surveys are quantitative and experiments test cause and effect.

t: A questionnaire asks respondents to indicate agreement with the statement 'My insurer settles claims promptly' on a five-point scale from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree'. This is a:
o: Ranking scale
Likert scale
Semantic differential scale
Dichotomous question
e: Likert scales measure degree of agreement with statements; a semantic differential uses bipolar adjectives such as 'fast–slow'.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018 the minimum capital requirement for a direct broker is:
o: ₹5 crore
₹4 crore
₹25 lakh
₹75 lakh
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Direct brokers need ₹75 lakh, reinsurance brokers ₹4 crore and composite brokers ₹5 crore.

t: The first step in the marketing research process is:
o: Designing the sample
Analysing and presenting findings
Collecting the data
Defining the problem and research objectives
e: A poorly defined problem wastes the rest of the process; design, collection and analysis follow problem definition.

t: An insurer offers a single standard motor policy to the whole market with one mass-media campaign. Its targeting strategy is:
o: Undifferentiated (mass) marketing
Micromarketing
Differentiated marketing
Concentrated (niche) marketing
e: Undifferentiated marketing ignores segment differences; differentiated marketing uses separate offers for several segments and concentrated marketing focuses on one.

t: To overcome the intangibility of insurance, a marketer should most appropriately:
o: Avoid any written documentation to keep things simple
Provide tangible cues such as a professional office, clear documents and well-presented staff
Rely entirely on word of mouth
Reduce premiums below cost
e: Because the service cannot be seen before purchase, customers judge quality from physical evidence; 'tangibilising the intangible' is a core services-marketing strategy.

t: Jan Carlzon used the term 'moments of truth' to describe:
o: Every instance in which a customer comes into contact with the organisation and forms an impression of its service
The moment a claim is finally paid
The point at which a service firm breaks even
The annual review of service standards by management
e: Each contact—an agent's call, a helpline conversation, a claim visit—is a moment of truth that builds or damages the customer's perception.

t: In a market where total annual general insurance premium is ₹2,80,000 crore, an insurer writing ₹14,000 crore has a market share of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Market share = 14,000 ÷ 2,80,000 = 0.05 = 5%.

t: In the services marketing triangle, the interaction between front-line employees and customers is called:
o: External marketing
Relationship marketing
Interactive marketing
Internal marketing
e: External marketing is the company's promises to customers, internal marketing enables employees to keep those promises, and interactive marketing is the actual delivery at the point of contact.

t: The SERVQUAL dimension 'empathy' is best demonstrated by an insurer that:
o: Gives individual attention and understands each customer's specific needs
Employs staff with professional qualifications
Pays claims exactly on the promised date
Has modern, attractive branch offices
e: Empathy is caring, individualised attention; the other options describe tangibles, reliability and assurance.

t: Free accidental-death cover of ₹1 lakh bundled with a two-wheeler policy, a 24x7 helpline and cashless garage access together constitute the:
o: Core product
Augmented product
Potential product
Generic product
e: The augmented product comprises additional services and benefits that exceed customer expectations and differentiate the offer from competitors.

t: In new-product development, the stage at which an insurer offers a product in a few selected branches or cities before a national launch is called:
o: Idea screening
Test marketing
Concept testing
Business analysis
e: Test marketing evaluates the product and its marketing programme under real conditions in a limited area; concept testing uses prospects' reactions to a description.

t: Price skimming is a strategy in which a firm:
o: Sets a low initial price to capture market share quickly
Prices below cost to drive out competitors
Matches the price of the market leader
Sets a high initial price to earn maximum margin from early buyers before gradually lowering it
e: Skimming suits innovative products with inelastic early demand; penetration pricing is the opposite approach.

t: A group personal accident policy covers 400 employees for ₹10 lakh each. The insurer's pure premium rate is ₹0.60 per ₹1,000 sum insured and expenses and profit are loaded at 20% on the pure premium. The total office premium is:
e: Total sum insured = 400 × ₹10 lakh = ₹40 crore; pure premium = 40,00,00,000 ÷ 1,000 × 0.60 = ₹2,40,000; add 20% loading = ₹2,88,000.

t: Under IRDAI's Point of Sales Person (PoSP) framework, which statement is correct?
o: A PoSP is licensed by IRDAI directly for five years
A PoSP sells only simple, pre-underwritten products after a short training and examination conducted by the insurer or intermediary
A PoSP may sell any product including unit-linked plans
A PoSP must hold a graduate degree and pass the IRDAI broker examination
e: PoSPs handle standard products that need minimal underwriting; the minimum qualification is Class X and training is about 15 hours, with the sponsoring entity responsible for conduct.

t: An insurance web aggregator is an intermediary that:
o: Maintains a website displaying product information and comparisons of different insurers and passes leads to them
Issues policies in its own name as a composite broker
Acts as a reinsurance broker for online insurers
Underwrites policies on behalf of several insurers
e: Web aggregators compile and compare products and generate leads; they cannot underwrite or issue policies and must be registered with IRDAI.

t: An Insurance Marketing Firm (IMF) differs from a corporate agent chiefly because an IMF:
o: May also distribute other financial products such as mutual funds and pension products and undertake insurance servicing activities
Can represent an unlimited number of insurers
Can sell only life insurance
Is not required to employ any trained sales persons
e: IMFs, introduced in 2015, employ Insurance Sales Persons and may market insurance alongside other regulated financial products and provide survey and claims-related services.

t: A life insurer's 13th-month persistency ratio of 78% means that:
o: 78% of claims were settled within 13 months
78% of policies sold a year earlier were still in force (premium paid) at the 13th month
The insurer renewed 78% of its group contracts
78% of policies lapsed within the first year
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Persistency measures continuation of policies; 13th-month persistency of 78% implies 22% of policies lapsed or were surrendered in the first year.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 affects distribution practice because it provides that:
o: Commission must be paid within 15 days of premium receipt
Policies must be delivered within 30 days of issue
No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the prescribed manner
Agents may collect premium only by cheque
e: Section 64VB means an agent or intermediary cannot bind cover on credit; the premium must reach the insurer (or its authorised collector) before risk attaches.

t: IRDAI's 'Bima Vahak' guidelines of 2023 envisage a distribution channel that is:
o: A digital marketplace for buying and servicing policies
A reinsurance pool for crop insurance
A single standardised life-health-property combination product
A women-centric, field-force at the Gram Panchayat level to improve insurance inclusion in rural areas
e: Bima Vahak is the distribution leg of IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' vision; Bima Sugam is the marketplace and Bima Vistaar the combination product.

t: An agent sold 120 policies last year and 48 of these came from referrals by existing customers. If the insurer's cost of acquiring a referred customer is ₹800 and of a non-referred customer is ₹2,000, the agent's average acquisition cost per policy was:
In the communication process model, 'noise' refers to:
o: Any interference that distorts the message between sender and receiver
The volume at which a radio advertisement is broadcast
The medium chosen to carry the message
The feedback sent by the receiver to the sender
e: Noise includes competing advertisements, distractions and misunderstanding; it is the reason messages should be simple and repeated.

t: A 'pull' promotion strategy in insurance marketing means the insurer:
o: Advertises directly to consumers so that they ask agents or banks for the product
Reduces premiums to attract intermediaries
Withdraws a product from the market
Offers higher incentives to agents to push the product to customers
e: Pull strategies create end-customer demand that draws the product through the channel; push strategies direct effort and incentives at the intermediaries.

t: An insurer buys 2,50,000 impressions on a news website for ₹75,000. The cost per thousand impressions (CPM) is:
Which of the following is an example of sales promotion rather than advertising?
o: A hoarding at a railway station
A full-page newspaper advertisement for a new term plan
A 30-second television commercial on a sports channel
Waiver of the first month's premium for policies bought during a festival fortnight
e: Sales promotion consists of short-term incentives to stimulate immediate purchase; the other options are paid mass-media advertising.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: The ladder of customer loyalty moves a person through the stages prospect, customer, client, supporter, advocate and finally:
o: Promoter
Agent
Shareholder
Partner
e: At the partner stage the customer and firm work together for mutual benefit; an advocate actively recommends the firm to others.

t: A health insurer had 50,000 policies due for renewal in a year and renewed 41,000 of them. Its renewal (retention) rate and lapse rate are respectively:
RFM analysis, used in customer relationship management, segments customers on the basis of:
o: Recency of purchase, frequency of purchase and monetary value
Region, family size and mobility
Risk, finance and marketing
Retention, feedback and motivation
e: RFM ranks customers on how recently and how often they buy and how much they spend, helping insurers prioritise cross-selling and retention efforts.

t: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), the life cover of ₹2 lakh is available to bank account holders aged 18 to 50 for an annual premium of:
e: PMJJBY premium was revised from ₹330 to ₹436 per annum from June 2022; ₹20 is the PMSBY accident-cover premium.

t: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provides:
o: Crop loss cover for notified crops
₹5 lakh hospitalisation cover per family per year
₹2 lakh life cover for natural or accidental death for ₹436 per annum
₹2 lakh for accidental death or total permanent disability and ₹1 lakh for partial permanent disability, for ₹20 per annum
e: PMSBY is an accident policy for persons aged 18 to 70 with auto-debit from a bank account; PMJJBY is the life cover and PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh health cover.

t: The 'social sector' for the purpose of insurers' obligations includes:
o: Only government employees
Only persons covered under group policies
Persons in the unorganised and informal sectors and economically vulnerable or backward classes, in both rural and urban areas
Only persons living in villages with population below 5,000
e: The social sector is defined by occupation and economic vulnerability, not geography, and so includes urban informal-sector workers.

t: Which of the following is the most effective way of reducing the distribution cost of a low-ticket rural insurance product?
o: Insisting on medical examination for every proposer
Advertising on national English-language television
Deploying individual agents to call on each household
Selling through group mechanisms such as self-help groups and co-operatives
e: Group distribution spreads fixed costs over many lives and uses existing trust networks; individual agency is uneconomic for premiums of a few hundred rupees.

t: Ivy Lee's 'Declaration of Principles' of 1906 is regarded as a milestone in public relations because it committed the practitioner to:
o: Supplying the press with accurate, prompt and open information rather than concealment
Refusing all contact with the media
Issuing advertisements disguised as news
Paying journalists for favourable coverage
e: Lee argued that the public should be informed, laying the foundation of PR as honest two-way communication rather than press agentry.

t: A house journal or in-house magazine is primarily a tool for communicating with which public?
o: Employees and the internal organisation
The regulator
Competitors
The financial press
e: House journals build internal morale, share company news and keep staff aligned with the organisation's goals; they are a key internal PR tool.

t: Advertising Value Equivalent (AVE) as a measure of PR effectiveness calculates:
o: The percentage of positive versus negative mentions
The increase in sales attributable to a press release
What the editorial coverage obtained would have cost if the same space or time had been bought as advertising
The number of journalists attending a press conference
e: AVE is widely criticised (and rejected by the Barcelona Principles) because it ignores the tone and credibility of coverage, but it is still a commonly cited metric.

t: Which of the following best distinguishes corporate 'image' from corporate 'reputation'?
o: They are identical terms
Image concerns products while reputation concerns prices
Image is created only by advertising while reputation is created only by PR
Image is the immediate impression publics hold, while reputation is the enduring collective judgement built over time
e: Image can be shaped quickly by communication; reputation rests on consistent performance and conduct and is harder to build or repair.

t: An insurer sponsors a city marathon and ensures its logo appears on bibs, banners and media coverage. This PR activity is best described as:
o: Crisis communication
Sponsorship aimed at building brand visibility and goodwill
Lobbying
Investor relations
e: Sponsorship associates the brand with an event or cause valued by its publics; lobbying addresses policymakers and investor relations addresses shareholders.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
o: Section 140
Section 146
Section 163A
Section 166
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Under IRDAI's Protection of Policyholders' Interests framework in force from 2024, the free-look period available to a policyholder is:
o: 7 days from the date of proposal
30 days from the date of receipt of the policy document, for all policies
15 days, extended to 30 days only for policies sold online
15 days for all policies
e: The 2024 regulations extended the free-look period to 30 days uniformly; earlier it was 15 days (30 days for electronic/distance-marketed policies).

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Under IRDAI's grievance redressal norms, an insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within:
o: Six months of its receipt
90 days of its receipt
Two weeks (14 days) of its receipt
24 hours of its receipt
e: Grievances must be acknowledged promptly and resolved within 14 days; unresolved complaints can be escalated through the Bima Bharosa portal and then to the Insurance Ombudsman.

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 established the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), which can act against:
o: Reinsurance treaty terms
Misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices affecting consumers as a class
Insurers' solvency shortfalls
Agents' examination results
e: The CCPA can order discontinuation of misleading advertisements and impose penalties on manufacturers, service providers and endorsers; prudential matters remain with IRDAI.
